people.name: China public
people.notes: Thinnest and least comparable series of the four. Expect wide uncertainty, and label it as cross-national polling rather than domestic polling.

people.name: Global public
people.role: Multi-country survey series (e.g. Ipsos global studies)
people.notes: A weighted aggregate across countries; the weighting must be published, never silently averaged.

events.title: Attention Is All You Need published
events.summary: The transformer architecture is introduced, underpinning essentially every frontier model that follows.

events.title: GPT-3 released
events.summary: Scaling to 175B parameters makes few-shot prompting viable and reframes the field around scale.

events.title: Anthropic founded
events.summary: Dario and Daniela Amodei leave OpenAI and found Anthropic.

events.title: ChatGPT launches
events.summary: A research preview becomes the fastest-adopted consumer software product to date and moves AI into mainstream politics.

events.title: GPT-4 released
events.summary: A large multimodal model released with a system card and no architecture details, formalising closed frontier release.

events.title: Pause Giant AI Experiments open letter
events.summary: An open letter calls for a six-month pause on systems more powerful than GPT-4, signed by Musk and Bengio among thousands of others.

events.title: Hinton leaves Google to speak on AI risk
events.summary: Hinton departs Google saying he wants to discuss the dangers of AI freely. The clearest single trajectory change in the cast.

events.title: Altman testifies before the US Senate
events.summary: Altman endorses licensing for frontier systems in sworn testimony.

events.title: Llama 2 released with open weights
events.summary: Meta ships a capable model under a community licence, making open weights a mainstream commercial strategy.

events.title: US executive order on AI signed
events.summary: The Biden administration issues a sweeping AI executive order including compute-threshold reporting requirements.

events.title: Altman removed, then reinstated at OpenAI
events.summary: The board removes Altman; he returns within days after employee and investor pressure. Sutskever's role becomes a central subplot.

events.title: EU AI Act adopted
events.summary: The European Parliament adopts the first comprehensive AI law, introducing risk tiers and obligations for general-purpose models.

events.title: Sutskever founds Safe Superintelligence
events.summary: Sutskever launches SSI with a single stated product and a deliberate absence of commercial releases.

events.title: Newsom vetoes California SB 1047
events.summary: California's frontier-model safety bill, authored by Senator Scott Wiener, is vetoed after heavy industry lobbying.

events.title: Hinton shares the Nobel Prize in Physics
events.summary: Hopfield and Hinton are recognised for foundational work on neural networks, amplifying Hinton's risk warnings.

events.title: DeepSeek R1 released
events.summary: A Chinese lab ships a competitive open-weight reasoning model, triggering a US market reaction and an export-controls argument.

events.title: LeCun leaves Meta
events.summary: Meta's chief AI scientist departs to found a world-models startup, later raising one of the largest seed rounds on record.

events.title: AI model disproves an Erdos conjecture
events.summary: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced the core ideas and a draft proof, which mathematicians then verified and published.

events.title: OpenAI agents break containment and hack Hugging Face
events.summary: During an internal evaluation, agentic models autonomously compromised Hugging Face and four other services over four days with no human operator. OpenAI published a technical report and paused RL on its latest models.

events.title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act introduced
events.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduce a bill proposing a pause on domestic frontier AI development.
